nodes.name: TRO/RKLTO
nodes.formula: (K0.469La0.531)TiO3 with surface Ru-doping and Ti-doped RuO2 nanoparticles

nodes.name: KLTO Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 3 mmol Ti(SO4)2 and 2 mmol La(NO3)3·6H2O were added into 20 mL of 8 M KOH solution, which was then magnetically stirred for ~2 h to obtain a white suspension. Subsequently, the white suspension was transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave, sealed, and heated at 200 °C for 20 h. The white product was filtered and washed with 0.1 M dilute hydrochloric acid to remove undesired La(OH)3 species. The product was rinsed with deionized water and ethyl alcohol, and dried in an oven at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the resulting product was ground to a fine powder for further use.

nodes.source_text: The K0.469La0.531TiO3 (KLTO) substrate was synthesized by a hydrothermal process according to our previously reported method.28 Briefly, 3 mmol Ti(SO4)2 and 2 mmol La(NO3)3·6H2O were added into 20 mL of 8 M KOH solution... ground to a fine powder for further use.

nodes.name: TRO/RKLTO Hydrothermal Decoration
nodes.procedure: 0.48 mmol (0.1 g) RuCl3·xH2O was dissolved in deionized water to form a homogeneous solution (pH = 1-2). Then, the appropriate amount of the as-prepared KLTO was added into the above solution and stirred for 30 min. The resulting mixture was transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave and placed in an oven at 120 °C for 12 h. The precipitate was collected and washed with deionized water several times, and then dried under a vacuum at 60 °C for 12 h.

nodes.procedure: RuO2 and KLTO were dispersed in deionized water, while concentrated hydrochloric acid was employed to adjust the pH value (1–2). The obtained sample was marked as RuO2/KLTO.

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction peaks consistent with cubic KLTO (Pm3m, JCPDS 89-4930) without detectable impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of KLTO reveals that all diffraction peaks are consistent with the cubic (K0.469La0.531)TiO3 (KLTO, Pm3m, JCPDS 89-4930) without detectable impurities (Fig. S2, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms existence of Ru element in TRO/RKLTO (Fig. S3 and Table S1, ESI†).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) confirms the existence of the Ru element in the final sample (Fig. S3 and Table S1, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content of 17.42 wt% in TRO/RKLTO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) measurements indicate 17.42 wt% of Ru in TRO/RKLTO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lower K-L2,3 edge intensity and significant Ru-M4,5 edge at surface confirm K replacement by Ru; Ti4+ (TiHO) in substrate, Ti3+ (TiLO) in nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Obviously, a much lower intensity of the K-L2,3 edge and a significant Ru-M4,5 edge in the B region demonstrate that the surface K of the KLTO substrate is replaced by the Ru element.

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 75.4 m2 g-1 from layered KLTO nanosheets (Fig. S8 and S9, ESI†).
nodes.evidence_snippet: TRO/RKLTO shows a large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 75.4 m2 g-1 (Fig. S8 and S9, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3d peaks at 280.8 eV (Ru4+ 3d5/2) and 282.3 eV (Ru5+ 3d5/2); Ti 2p at 458.4 eV and 464.1 eV (Ti4+).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The two peaks located at 280.8 and 282.3 eV correspond to Ru4+ 3d5/2 and Ru5+ 3d5/2... The XPS binding energy of 458.4 and 464.1 eV for Ti 2p is attributed to Ti4+ 2p3/2 and Ti4+ 2p1/2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge absorption edge of TRO/RKLTO close to RuO2; Ti K-edge shows mainly 4+ valence identical to bulk KLTO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2b shows the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of TRO/RKLTO, Ru and RuO2. It is obvious that the absorption edge of TRO/RKLTO is close to that of RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS Ru-O shell at 1.99 Å (vs 1.96 Å in RuO2); Ru-O coordination number 3.22 (Table S2, ESI†).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectrum (non-phase shift corrected) of TRO/RKLTO shows a main peak, which is fitted by a Ru-O shell with a bond distance of 1.99 Å... The coordination number (CN) of Ru-O was found to be 3.22.
